composition.serve_who: This sheet (GMMS 108'-114b, "BILGE / WATER VALVE SYSTEM") is a relay/terminal wiring sheet for five 24V DC motor-operated fresh-water valves/pumps, each identically wired: Fresh Water Valve, Fresh Water Port Bunker, Fresh Water Stbd Bunker, Fresh Water Port Suction, Fresh Water Stbd Suction. All are supplied from a common WATER TRANSFER VALVES Q14 10A breaker fed from +24V SERVICE BAT. via F6 300A fuse, through terminal strip T/S B. Per the engineer-confirmed mapping, WATER TRANSFER VALVES -> 510-water-transfer-valves, so all five OPEN/CLOSE valve/pump-motor control loops on this sheet serve that node. XA60 pin taps are CONTROL INs (they land on the OPEN/CLOSE switch contacts driving each motor circuit) and XA41 pin taps are STATUS OUTs (they are taken off the relay coil/return side of each loop) — this matches established ONYX-monitoring conventions (XA-style taps) but the exact remote system (ONYX) is a cross-reference, not drawn here.

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Load name 'FRESH WATER VALVE' on the M-symbol matches the engineer-confirmed mapping WATER TRANSFER VALVES -> 510-water-transfer-valves; the whole T/S B/Re7/terminals 51-55 group feeds this single load.

functions.label: Fresh Water Valve open/close control loop
functions.what_it_does: Remotely opens or closes the motor-operated Fresh Water Valve via relay Re7, using terminals 51-55 on T/S B; relay Re7 also provides a status tap back to the monitoring system.

flow_scenarios.path: +24V SERVICE BAT. -> F6 300A fuse -> Q14 10A breaker (WATER TRANSFER VALVES) -> T/S B terminal 14 (fused terminal, feeds Re7 contact common)
XA60 pin 02 -> terminal 51 (pin 1) -> OPEN contact closes -> motor M (Fresh Water Valve) pin 1 energised to drive valve open
XA60 pin 04 -> terminal 52 (pin 4) -> CLOSE contact closes -> motor M (Fresh Water Valve) pin 4 energised to drive valve closed
Re7 contact (common from T/S B-14) -> terminals 53(pin3)/54(pin2) -> motor M runs valve actuator; Re7 coil return -> terminal 55 -> XA41 pin 10 status tap to monitoring

key_components: Re7 relay (coil/contact, NO/NC not legibly distinguished on this sheet)

infrastructure.system_name: Water Transfer Valves 24V DC supply/distribution (T/S B, Q14, F6)
facts: Supply chain: +24V SERVICE BAT. -> F6 300A fuse -> Q14 10A breaker labelled 'WATER TRANSFER VALVES' -> terminal strip T/S B

T/S B distributes to terminals 14/15/16/17/18, each feeding one of the five relays Re7-Re11 (one per valve); T/S B terminals 14 and 15 are marked with built-in fuses (fused terminal, troubleshooting culprits)

This matches established fact: [510-water-transfer-valves] electrical_supply Q14 10A, panel EMERGENCY POWER SUPPLY / EMERGENCY PANEL (GMMS 108-111) — consistent, same breaker id carried onto this sheet
+24V SERVICE BAT. negative/return side is not traced on this sheet (only the positive path through F6/Q14 is drawn)

cross_references.what: XA60 pins 02/04/06/08/10/12/14/16/18/20 — command-in taps driving each valve's OPEN/CLOSE contacts
XA41 pins 10/12/14/16/18 — status-out taps reporting each relay's state to monitoring

uncertainties: Re7-Re11: whether the load (motor terminals 53/54, 58/59, 63/64, 68/69, 73/74) sits on the NC or NO contact of each relay is not legible on this sheet (contact=unknown in the measured netlist) — this determines whether the valve is normally-open or normally-closed on loss of relay power; needs engineer confirmation (echoes open question q13 from an earlier sheet).

Each relay coil's negative/return side beyond terminal 55/60/65/70/75 (i.e., whether it truly returns to a negative bus or is purely a status tap to XA41) is not fully distinguishable from a supply/control conductor on this sheet.
good_to_have: Exact fuse rating of the built-in fuses on T/S B terminals 14/15 (and similarly 16/17/18) not printed — visible only as fuse symbol; capture at inspection if needed.
Part numbers/models for the five motor-operated valve actuators are not given on this sheet (see BOM cross-reference elsewhere, e.g. Burkert actuators noted on bilge-valves sheet).
discarded_as_clutter: Diamond-enclosed cross-reference numbers (e.g. '10 XA41', '12 XA41') — these are wire-tap callouts already captured as XA41/XA60 status/command taps, not separate devices
Title block repeated fields (DWG No., TITLE, DATE, DRAWN, copyright notice) — administrative metadata, not equipment
'T/S B' label repeats across all five rows — same physical terminal strip, captured once as infrastructure
Various unlabeled pin-number annotations ('1','2','3','4') that simply restate motor pin assignments already captured in flow scenarios
